text:
alex: Hi folks — got an EOB saying my ortho visit (5/12) was denied for 'no authorization on file'. I did see my PCP 2 days before but didn't explicitly ask for a referral number. Is that a lost cause or can it be fixed without rebooking?
maya (People Ops): Not necessarily lost. Two paths: 1) Get a retroactive authorization/referral from your PCP office (they can often create one and date it appropriately), then submit a claim correction/appeal to the insurer with that doc + EOB. 2) If PCP refuses, file an appeal with a supporting letter explaining the referral was verbally approved and include clinical notes — sometimes that works but takes longer.
alex: For path #1, what's the minimal paperwork Anthem needs? They have a tiny upload field on the portal and I don't want to miss fields.
maya (People Ops): Minimal set: EOB (PDF), the referral/authorization PDF or fax confirmation, and a one-paragraph cover note with these fields: claim number, date of service, provider name & NPI, auth/referral number, and your contact. Here

Small template you can paste into the portal:

Requesting claim correction for claim #<CLAIM_NUM>.
Date of service: <MM/DD/YYYY>.
Provider: <Dr. Name> (NPI <#####>).
PCP referral/auth number: <AUTH-XXXXX>.
Attached: EOB, referral/authorization.
Member contact: <phone/email>.

This hits the keywords their claims team searches for.
billing-bot: Reminder: Upload supporting docs via Benefits Portal -> Claims -> Upload Documents within 30 days of EOB to avoid auto-deny on refile.
anthem-support: Hi @alex 
We can reopen as a correction. Please DM member ID + claim number and attach the referral PDF or fax cover sheet. If you only have a PCP note, DM that too and we'll flag for manual review. Typical turnaround for manual review ~10-21 business days.
alex: Quick q 
Is 'pre-authorization' different from a 'PCP referral' for specialty visits? PCP just gave a verbal ok.
maya (People Ops): Good question. "Referral" is usually an administrative step from PCP to specialist; "prior authorization" is a payer process required for some services. For ortho consults, most plans want a PCP referral number — if Anthem treats it as an auth-required service they will need a prior auth number. If PCP gave only verbal ok, ask them to generate a written referral or submit an auth request to Anthem retroactively. Ask the office to include the date the verbal approval happened.
alex: Thanks all. I'll call the PCP billing desk, get whatever doc they can provide, scan and upload. @anthem-support I'll DM claim + member ID once I have it. Appreciate the fast help. :thumbsup:
